methods.label: Connect the circle centers
methods.explanation:
Connecting the centers turns the tangencies into known lengths. Let \(O\) be the center of the radius-\(13\) circle, and let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the centers of the small circles touching it at \(A\) and \(B\), respectively.

At a tangency point, both radii are perpendicular to the common tangent, so the centers and contact point are collinear. For internal tangency, \(P\) lies between \(O\) and \(A\), and \(Q\) lies between \(O\) and \(B\). Therefore
\[
OP=OQ=13-5=8.
\]
External tangency of the small circles gives \(PQ=5+5=10\).

Now \(OP\) and \(OA\) lie along the same ray, as do \(OQ\) and \(OB\). Consequently, triangles \(OPQ\) and \(OAB\) have the same included angle at \(O\), with
\[
\frac{OA}{OP}=\frac{OB}{OQ}=\frac{13}{8}.
\]
They are similar by SAS, so their corresponding third sides satisfy
\[
AB=\frac{13}{8}\,PQ=\frac{13}{8}\cdot10=\frac{65}{4}.
\]
Since \(65\) is odd, this fraction is in lowest terms. Thus \(m=65\), \(n=4\), and \(\boxed{m+n=69}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
